what: Like a desktop window — grab the handle on the window header and a window clone follows the pointer with .16s power4.out (the original window fades to .35), while a dotted slot snaps to a 20px grid (or the cell width) to preview where it will land. On release the original window moves into that slot, and the clone slides in from where it was over 1s cubic-bezier(.33,0,0,1)

options.cell: Vertical (or horizontal if there are no columns) grid spacing (px), default 20
options.cols: Number of cells to match the width to the cell width, default 0 (by grid)
options.follow: Length the clone trails behind (seconds), default .16
options.dur: Settling time after dropping (seconds), default 1 — reduce it if moved often like an app
options.[data-fx-part=win]: Window to move (placed inside the panel with left·top)

use:
Your window name here
…
note: Not applied on touch devices (the original also shows the handle only on wide screens). On release, fx:drop is applied to the panel{win,x,y}, fires fx:snap when the cell changes — catch it if you want to save the layout

from.where: index.js window drag (original widget grid — 12 cells · 20px grid · floatQuickX/Y quickTo .16 power4.out · Flip 1s original curve)
